question: Explain how the bending of light at a refracting surface is used in the formation of images by lenses. Give reason why a convex lens can converge parallel rays.

options.A: A convex lens converges parallel rays because it is thinner at the centre and thicker at the edges.
options.B: A convex lens converges parallel rays because light travels through it without refraction.
options.C: At each curved surface of a lens, light refracts because its speed changes between media. In a convex lens, the combined refraction bends parallel rays towards the principal axis so that they meet at the focus and form images.
options.D: A convex lens converges rays by total internal reflection from its curved surfaces.
